To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
discourse structure need bear the full burden for conveying discourse relations.

(1) discourse relations are grounded in anaphoric presupposition; (2) discourse structure is simplified by grounding discourse relations in the presupposition of an anaphor, rather than in the structure of the discourse; (3) the same lexicalised TAG machinery used to derive clause-level semantics is used to derive discourse structure.
discourse relations need not be represented structurally in a discourse representation structure (DRS), but can be represented in the form of anaphoric links between DRSs.

The main takeaway from our work is that
discourse relations can be grounded in the same lexical and structural resources used for clause-level semantics, and that this is a viable alternative to discourse structural accounts.
